Everything in this course runs on free, open-source software. Budget about
45 minutes for this page — spatial packages are large and compile slowly.

## 1. R

Install **R ≥ 4.3** from [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org/).

- **Windows** — download the `.exe`, accept the defaults.
- **macOS** — download the `.pkg` matching your chip (Apple silicon vs Intel).
- **Linux** — use your distribution's packages, or
  [r2u](https://eddelbuettel.github.io/r2u/) on Ubuntu for fast binary installs.

## 2. RStudio

Install **RStudio Desktop** from
[posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).
It bundles Quarto, so you do not need to install Quarto separately.

## 3. System libraries (Linux only)

`sf` and `terra` wrap the GDAL/GEOS/PROJ C++ libraries. macOS and Windows get
pre-built binaries; Linux usually needs the development headers first:

```bash
sudo apt install libgdal-dev libgeos-dev libproj-dev libudunits2-dev libssl-dev
```

## 4. R packages

Open RStudio and paste this into the console. It installs only what is
missing, so it is safe to rerun.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pkgs <- c(
  # --- spatial core (Sessions 2-3) ---
  "sf", "terra", "units", "ggspatial",
  # --- trajectories and metrics (Sessions 3-4) ---
  "amt", "adehabitatLT", "bcpa", "move2",
  # --- simulation (Session 5) ---
  "circular",
  # --- home ranges (Session 6) ---
  "adehabitatHR", "ctmm",
  # --- selection functions (Session 7) ---
  "survival",
  # --- hidden Markov models (Session 8) ---
  "momentuHMM",
  # --- wrangling and graphics ---
  "tidyverse", "lubridate", "patchwork",
  # --- environmental data (optional) ---
  "MODISTools",
  # --- documents ---
  "knitr", "rmarkdown"
)

missing <- pkgs[!vapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing)) install.packages(missing) else message("All set.")
```
:::


::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## If installation fails

**`sf` or `terra` fail to compile (Linux/macOS)** — you are missing the system
libraries in step 3. Install them, restart R, try again.

**`Warning: package 'X' is in use and will not be installed`** — restart R
(Session → Restart R) and rerun before loading anything.

**Everything is glacially slow** — you are compiling from source. On Windows
and macOS choose "no" when asked *"Do you want to install from sources the
package which needs compilation?"*.

**Corporate or university proxy blocks CRAN** — set a mirror explicitly:
`options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))`.
:::

## 5. Check your installation

Run this. If it prints a green-ish summary with no `MISSING` lines, you are
ready.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
need <- c("sf", "terra", "amt", "adehabitatLT", "adehabitatHR", "ctmm",
          "bcpa", "momentuHMM", "circular", "tidyverse", "ggspatial")
for (p in need) {
  ok <- requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("%-14s %s\n", p, if (ok) as.character(packageVersion(p)) else "MISSING"))
}

# GDAL / GEOS / PROJ must all report a version:
sf::sf_extSoftVersion()
```
:::


## 6. Get the course project

The tidiest way to work is to keep everything in one folder.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### With git (recommended)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/GiulianoColosimo/animtrack-2627.git
```

Then open `animtrack-2627.Rproj` in RStudio. You get every update with
`git pull`.

### Without git

Go to the
[repository](https://github.com/GiulianoColosimo/animtrack-2627),
click **Code → Download ZIP**, unzip it somewhere sensible (*not* inside a
syncing folder that renames files), and open the `.Rproj` file.

:::

Working inside the project means every path in the exercises —
`data/buffalo_kruger.csv.gz` and friends — resolves without you editing
anything.

## 7. A five-minute R refresher

If R is new to you, these are worth the evening:

- [R for Data Science (2e), chapters 1–5](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) — the
  standard introduction to the data-wrangling verbs used throughout.
- [Spatial Data Science with R and `terra`](https://rspatial.org/) — the
  reference for Sessions 2 and 3.
- [Geocomputation with R](https://r.geocompx.org/) — the best free GIS-in-R book.

The three things you must be comfortable with before Session 2:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
x <- c(1, 4, 9)         # assignment and vectors
df <- data.frame(a = x, b = sqrt(x))   # data frames
library(dplyr)          # loading a package
df |> filter(a > 1) |> mutate(c = a * b)   # the pipe
```
:::
